overview: The Medford City Council granted a special permit for a restaurant at 572 Boston Avenue, approved the first reading of a $2.12 million sewer improvement loan order, and heard extensive resident testimony concerning citywide traffic and pedestrian safety. The council also processed commercial licenses, discussed a newly signed ten-year Comcast contract, and approved various neighborhood resolutions.

items.title: Special Permit for 572 Boston Avenue
items.summary: The council approved a special permit application by CTDJ Incorporated to operate an eating establishment at 572 Boston Avenue.

items.title: Loan Order for City Sewer System Capital Improvements
items.summary: Following debate regarding project details and the use of water and sewer surplus funds, an amendment to fund a portion from retained earnings failed and the first reading of a $2,120,000 MWRA grant and loan appropriation passed.

items.title: Petition on Traffic Engineering and Street Safety
items.summary: Following testimony from numerous residents regarding speeding, cut-through traffic, and heavy trucks, the council approved a petition as amended to request speed bumps, signage, radar speed boards, and enhanced truck enforcement from the Traffic Commission and police.

items.title: Licences
items.summary: The council approved cleaning and dyeing licenses for Grace Cleaners and New Way Cleaners, as well as a taxi driver license for Louis St. Ange.

items.title: Medford Energy Committee Presentation
items.summary: Curtis Tuden presented on the Medford Green Awards and the upcoming Harvest Your Energy Festival, and the council placed the presentation on file.

items.title: Executive Session on Brooks Estate Caretaker Matter
items.summary: Following an executive session regarding the Brooks Estate caretaker matter, the council reconvened in open session and placed the update on file.

items.title: Maintenance at West Medford Commuter Rail Station
items.summary: The council approved a resolution requesting that the MBTA address weeding, stanchion replacement, and overall cleanliness at the West Medford station.

items.title: Zoning Review for Wellington Plaza
items.summary: The council passed a resolution asking the Office of Community Development to review zoning at Wellington Plaza to encourage transit-oriented, mixed-use commercial development and affordable housing.

items.title: Quarterly Budget Monitoring Meetings
items.summary: The council approved a resolution to meet quarterly as a committee of the whole with the budget director to review the operating budget.

items.title: Scaffolding and Building Conditions at 5 High Street
items.summary: The council approved an amended resolution requesting legal and building department action regarding prolonged scaffolding at 5 High Street and proposing a future ordinance to address long-term scaffolding.

items.title: Inquiry on Kiosk Parking Enforcement on July 4th
items.summary: The council approved a request for the Police Chief to report on parking tickets issued by Republic Parking on July 4th and to request Saturday office hours for the parking company.

items.title: Removal of Payphone Enclosures
items.summary: The council approved referring the removal of abandoned payphone stands, including one at 29 High Street, to the electrical department.

items.title: Condolence Resolutions
items.summary: The council adopted resolutions of condolence for the families of Salvatore DiMeo and Marie Ruberti.

items.title: Petition on Nonprofit Use of Library Space
items.summary: Resident Joe Viglione addressed the council regarding a directory for local nonprofits and their potential use of library facilities, which was received and placed on file.

items.title: Reappointment to Medford Housing Authority
items.summary: The council confirmed the mayor's reappointment of Michael Luongo to the Medford Housing Authority for a five-year term.

items.title: Comcast Cable Contract and PEG Access
items.summary: The council received and placed on file a copy of a newly signed ten-year Comcast contract, while an additional motion requesting a report from the mayor regarding PEG access at the high school failed to achieve the necessary four votes.
